comparator.sourceNotes: Full180EC prescribed membership is retained as research, including disputedQuantum6EC; active partial record withholds that unit.54EC specialisation is represented by tenindividualcourses, never added again.
components: Engineering the Building Blocks of Life

A compulsory team project follows the selected specialisation. Workshops and preparation run throughout the year, with execution in the final period. Practical participation requires the programme’s safety instruction.
Compulsory in the selected materials track; access for ST&I materials students remains unresolved.

A full-time eight-week team project develops a physical prototype through design, testing and ethical decisions. It ends with a demonstration, presentation and a partly individual defence. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project; practical work requires safety instruction.

An individual supervised research project includes a thesis and presentation and is examined by at least two UvA examiners. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project. External projects need Examination Board permission.

Thirty EC remain open for electives or a minor, normally in the first semester of year three. The study plan is assessed for overlap and approval; at most 12 EC may be introductory subjects, and a foreign minor needs prior approval.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialisation. The official curriculum presents three equally substantial 54-EC year-2 tracks and does not establish one as the general route. High-tech Designer Materials appears first, so it is selected as a neutral tie-break independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Sustainable technology, materials & design
alternatives.concept: Investigate sustainable materials and resource systems using chemical and mechanical foundations, circular recovery laboratories, environmental models and explicit product-design methods. Evaluate energy, lifecycle and stakeholder consequences; this related science/design response does not reproduce a full materials-physics specialisation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is organised around sustainable technical systems, materials, quantitative analysis, design and applied research rather than claiming a dedicated engineering degree.
progression: Current formal prerequisites/offerings pass;8advanced courses. Foundations support later disciplinary methods and design. SustainableDeltaResearch is only planned2026h2 and has noformalprerequisite; its variable partner task is not claimed to be a later specialist thesis. Open sequencing is not converted into a new hard requirement.

alternatives.label: Digital modelling, robotics & prototyping
alternatives.concept: Develop computational models and intelligent systems through software, algorithms, learning, signals and robotics. Connect them to material testing and consumer-product design, while evaluating sustainable and responsible implementation. Specific hardware fabrication is limited to what the actual selected courses support.
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, mathematical modelling, simulation, robotics and design form the visible spine, with both digital and physical prototype work.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces most earth, environmental, materials and circular-economy study with software development, computer vision, robotics, algorithms, reinforcement learning, optimisation and engineering mathematics. It differs by well over 30 EC and centres digital system design.
progression: Current formal prerequisites/offerings pass;9advanced courses. Foundations support later disciplinary methods and design. SustainableDeltaResearch is only planned2026h2 and has noformalprerequisite; its variable partner task is not claimed to be a later specialist thesis. Open sequencing is not converted into a new hard requirement.

alternatives.label: Life, health & bioinnovation
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory science, health and disease with programming, data, quantitative methods, product design, sustainability and applied research for biotechnology and health-oriented innovation.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme visibly integrates life-science mechanisms and laboratory work with health applications, quantitative tools and innovation projects.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from the environmental/materials and digital-system programmes by replacing most geoscience, circular-systems and advanced computing content with molecular cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work, anatomy, pharmacology, immunity and disease mechanisms. It passes the 30-EC distinctness floor against both earlier programmes.

core: Applied integration of science, technology and innovation to address practical societal challenges
Engineering design, iterative prototyping, testing and technical feasibility analysis
Programming, data analysis, quantitative methods, scientific modelling and simulation
Broad natural-science foundations spanning materials, physics, chemistry, biology, biochemistry, energy and environmental systems
Research expertise, responsible innovation, collaboration, communication and evidence-based technology assessment
High-tech Designer Materials: structure, composition, properties and design of smart and functional materials
adjacent: Sustainability, circularity, renewable energy, life-cycle thinking and technical transition design
Digital modelling, simulation, robotics, electronics and computational prototype development
Engineering life and health through biotechnology, cell biology, biochemistry and biomedical applications
questions: How can materials, energy and environmental systems be designed for sustainability and circularity?
How can models, simulations and digital or physical prototypes test whether a technological solution will work?
How can biological and biochemical mechanisms be translated into useful health or biotechnology applications?

blocks: Science, materials, energy and sustainable systems
Both study wave behaviour and material-related physical principles; the external component extends through light and quantum foundations.
Both investigate energy technologies and evaluate sustainable systems. UCR emphasises technical/economic energy assessment; the external course adds chemical energy-storage and reaction foundations.
Data, modelling, simulation and intelligent systems
Relational databases, SQL and querying overlap with the external client-server/data course; interactive JavaScript/front-end work is not supplied by this UCR course.
Both introduce machine-learning methods and evaluation. The external course specifically applies them to scientific/molecular/material problems; UCR does not guarantee those applications.
Both develop programming and computational problem solving for scientific models; specialised scientific applications differ.
Both develop mathematical foundations for quantitative scientific problems; the external course contextualises these across ST&I themes.
Both develop eigenvalues, matrices and linear-system reasoning. The external course also develops vector calculus and differential equations beyond this UCR course.
Signals, transfer functions, filters and frequency-domain analysis overlap with the electronics component. UCR does not supply the full circuit-building/photonics laboratory.
Both develop statistical data analysis; probability/inference provides a substantive methodological overlap, without asserting identical software or datasets.
Both develop molecular/cellular/biochemical foundations of living systems; disciplinary scope and practical activities differ.

Both use molecular cloning/transformation, PCR and DNA/protein laboratory techniques. The external component additionally covers specific genome-engineering and synthetic-network methods not established here.
Design, responsible innovation and applied research
Both develop academic inquiry, collaboration, communication and reflection. UCR does not reproduce the full external Makerspace technical-skills component.

Both use iterative design, specifications and project development toward a product. UCR prototypes are developed where feasible, while the external compulsory team project follows a technical specialisation.

selection.assessment: Sequentially reconsider the strongest materials/sustainable-design response, then digital modelling/physical-interface questions, then life/health mechanisms and laboratory inquiry. Course-set differences are substantive consequences, not automatic acceptance from numerical floors. Three conditional trials survive for research, but full comparability, candidate acceptance and stopping remain unverified while access to compulsoryQuantum6EC is unresolved. No fourth default option or no-match; the separate SustainabilityCircularity concept overlaps strongly with the closest route and is not accepted merely because a formaltrack exists.

notes.text: The selected external route includes a 54 EC materials specialisation, sustained physical prototyping and an individual 18 EC research project. UCR research directions provide specific science, computation, circular-resource, life-laboratory and design contributions. Dedicated quantum and condensed-matter depth, instrumentation and the full physical prototype studio remain important limits. No professional engineering equivalence or complete pathway is certified.

audience.programmeDescription: Science, Technology & Innovation at the University of Amsterdam is a Dutch-taught programme combining natural sciences, data and modelling with the design and testing of technological prototypes. This example follows High-tech Designer Materials.
audience.comparisonExplanation: These UCR directions remain provisional while access to compulsory Quantum Physics 1 is confirmed. The active external record shows the supported 174 EC subset.

curriculum.limitation: The confirmed list accounts for 174 credits. Quantum Physics 1 is required in the materials track, but its course-entry rule does not list students from this programme. Access to that six-credit requirement still needs confirmation.
